title: Why the Soviet Union Broke Into Exactly 15 Countries
voice: Platform TTS; American English documentary narration

paragraphs.text: On December twenty-fifth, nineteen ninety-one, the red flag fell over the Kremlin. By the next day, the Soviet Union was gone: fifteen states. Why exactly fifteen? The answer was in its map.
In nineteen twenty-two, four republics formed the Union: Russia, Ukraine, Belarus, Transcaucasia. The treaty let each leave; smaller autonomous republics had no exit.
In nineteen thirty-six, Stalin set three tests: an external border, a compact titular majority, and over one million people. Tatarstan had more people than Estonia, but no foreign border.
The Baltic republics were annexed in nineteen forty. Karelo-Finnish made sixteen; its nineteen fifty-six demotion restored fifteen, with the constitutional right to secede.
In nineteen ninety-one, fifteen union republics became independent states on Soviet borders. Smaller units had no matching exit. The founders drew the seams that split the Union.
